formation.note: ATLAS marked its 30th anniversary on 1 October 2022, consistent with this date; INSPIRE's experiment record gives date_proposed 1992-10-01.
formation.quote: Submitted on 1 October 1992 (being considered the birthdate of the collaboration), the Letter of Intent was a 108-page document which made the physics case for a general purpose proton-proton experiment at the LHC.

country_count.note: The collaboration page and the official institutions list both give 40 countries (list: 'Number of countries with ATLAS institutions: 40', read 2026-10-25); CERN's ATLAS page gave 42 countries in March 2022.

institution_count.display: 175 institutions (246 institutes counting cluster members and associates)
institution_count.locator: atlaspo.cern.ch/public/institutions, summary block at the foot of the page (Number of countries 40; Total number of institutions 175: Regular institutions 154, Cluster institutions 21; Institutes in clusters 76; Associate institutes 16; Total number of institutes 246). The page carries no date of its own beyond its footer; read 2026-10-25.
institution_count.note: This is the official ATLAS institutions list's own total. The collaboration's page atlas.cern/Discover/Collaboration gives the rounded headline '170+ Institutions' (read 2026-10-25), consistent with 175. The list counts 175 institutions (154 regular institutions and 21 clusters of institutes) and 246 institutes (the 154, the 76 institutes inside the clusters and 16 associates); it also lists 19 technical associates and 10 Tier-1 computing centres, which are not counted in either total. The Atlas holds 197 institution rows from the list as read on 2026-09-17 (see the roster snapshot), so those rows are institutes, not institutions, and they are not a complete copy of the list's 246.

member_count.note: Lower bound ('over 5500'). The same sentence gives 3000 scientific authors; the page also states 1200 doctoral students.

name: ATLAS Collaboration
notes: Sizes from three official ATLAS pages, read 2026-10-25. The collaboration page (atlas.cern/Discover/Collaboration) says 'over 5500 members and 3000 scientific authors', '170+ Institutions', '40 Countries'. The official institutions list (atlaspo.cern.ch/public/institutions) counts 175 institutions, 246 institutes and 40 countries. CERN's ATLAS page gave 'More than 5500 scientists from 245 institutes in 42 countries' in March 2022. The institution figures differ only in what they count: institutions (175; '170+' on the collaboration page) versus institutes (246 on the list, 245 in 2022), where cluster members and associates count as institutes.
The Atlas's 197 institution rows come from the official institutions list as read on 2026-09-17; they are institutes (a subset of the list's 246), not a count of institutions.
The page gives its counts without a date; the membership 'as of' month (2026-09) is when the roster was recorded. The figures are lower bounds where the page says 'over' or '170+'.
Leadership rows are empty: no source consulted names the current spokesperson.

summary.plain: The international team that built and runs the ATLAS experiment. It counts its birthday as 1 October 1992, the day it handed CERN its Letter of Intent, and today it has more than 5500 members from over 170 institutions in about 40 countries.
summary.technical: Collaboration operating experiment:atlas at CERN LHC Point 1. Founded 1 October 1992 with the submission of the ATLAS Letter of Intent to the LHC Experiments Committee. Governed by a Collaboration Board that elects the Spokesperson for renewable two-year terms.
